definition: Guided local search is a metaheuristic search method.
details: A meta-heuristic method is a method that sits on top of a local search algorithm to change its behavior. Guided local search builds up penalties during a search. It uses penalties to help local search algorithms escape from local minima and plateaus. When the given local search algorithm settles in a local optimum, GLS modifies the objective function using a specific scheme (explained below). Then the local search will operate using an augmented objective function, which is designed to bring the search out of the local optimum. The key is in the way that the objective function is modified. The method in its current form was developed by Dr Christos Voudouris and detailed in his PhD Thesis. GLS was inspired by and extended GENET, a neural network architecture for solving Constraint Satisfaction Problems, which was developed by Chang Wang, Edward Tsang and Andrew Davenport. Both GLS's and GENET's mechanism for escaping from local minima resembles reinforcement learning.

explainer.lead: Guided local search helps an ordinary local search algorithm stop circling around answers that are good nearby but not good enough overall. It adds penalties as the search proceeds, changing the objective so the algorithm can escape local minima and plateaus.

tiers.eli5: When your search keeps getting stuck in the same spot, this method adds small penalties to well-worn choices so you are nudged to try somewhere else.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers wrap it around a local search, building penalties during the run that modify the objective; a pitfall is poor tuning of the penalty scheme, which can distort the search away from good solutions.
tiers.paperLevel: A metaheuristic that accumulates penalties during search; when the local search settles at a local optimum, GLS modifies the objective function by a specific scheme, and the local search then operates on the augmented objective function designed to bring improvement. Known limits: the given facts do not state convergence guarantees or optimality bounds.

explainer.example: Suppose a route-search procedure minimizes travel cost and stops at route A with cost 10 because every neighboring route looks worse. GLS adds penalties to the objective, making the augmented cost of staying around A less attractive, so local search moves to a neighboring route B. Continuing from B, it reaches route C with an original cost of 8, an improvement that was inaccessible while the search remained trapped at A.
explainer.goal: To help a local search algorithm escape local minima and plateaus by accumulating penalties and searching with an augmented objective function.
outputs: A candidate solution produced by the continued search
An objective augmented with accumulated penalties
steps: Run local search using the original objective function.
Notice when the search settles at a local optimum or becomes stuck on a plateau.
Build up penalties and modify the objective according to the GLS scheme.
Resume local search using the augmented objective.
Continue modifying the objective as needed to guide the search out of further traps.
tradeoffs: Penalties create a way out of local optima, but the search still depends on the underlying local search algorithm.
The augmented objective guides exploration and can differ from the original objective being optimized.
Its effectiveness depends on how the objective is modified with penalties.
